10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001.title: Help things become new
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001.intro: An old bottle can become something new. Let's learn how to help!

facts.title: Empty and rinse
facts.body: Ask a grown-up to help empty and rinse the bottle.

facts.title: No bag
facts.body: Put items in the recycling bin one at a time. Do not put them in a plastic bag.

facts.title: Ask first
facts.body: Different places have different bin rules. Ask your teacher or a grown-up which items can go in.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001.question: How should we put empty bottles in the recycling bin?
choices: One at a time, with no bag
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001.explanation: Yes! Put empty bottles in one at a time, with no bag. This helps the machines sort them.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.title: Where do bags go?
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.intro: A plastic bag is soft and thin. It needs a different place from a bottle.

facts.title: Bags can get stuck
facts.body: Plastic bags can wrap around the machines that sort recycling.

facts.title: A special place
facts.body: Some stores have a bin just for clean plastic bags. A grown-up can check for you.

facts.title: Ask for help
facts.body: Keep bags out of your home recycling bin. Ask a grown-up what to do with them.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.question: Where could a clean plastic bag go?
choices: In a store's special bag bin
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.explanation: Yes! Ask a grown-up to find a store that takes clean plastic bags.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003.title: Keep paper clean
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003.intro: Clean paper can become new paper. Food and grease can make that harder.

facts.title: Look at the box
facts.body: A pizza box may have oily spots. That oil is called grease.

facts.title: Keep grease out
facts.body: Grease makes the paper dirty. Keep greasy parts out of paper recycling.

facts.title: A grown-up can help
facts.body: Ask a grown-up to check the rules for your box. Do not pick through a trash bin.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003.question: Why do we keep greasy paper out of paper recycling?
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003.explanation: Yes! Grease makes paper dirty. Clean paper is easier to turn into new paper.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004.title: Food helps plants grow
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004.intro: Some food scraps can become compost. Compost helps plants grow!

facts.title: Save some scraps
facts.body: Fruit peels and bits of vegetables can go in a compost bin. Ask a grown-up which bin to use.

facts.title: Add dry leaves
facts.body: A compost pile needs dry things too. Dry leaves help balance wet food scraps.

facts.title: Leave plastic out
facts.body: Take stickers and wrappers off food with a grown-up's help. Plastic does not belong in the pile.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004.question: Which dry thing can help a compost pile?
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004.explanation: Yes! Dry leaves help the pile turn food scraps into compost.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005.title: Get jars and cans ready
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005.intro: A jar or a can can become something new. A grown-up can help get it ready.

facts.title: Empty first
facts.body: Ask a grown-up to empty any food or drink left inside.

facts.title: Give it a rinse
facts.body: A quick rinse helps wash away bits of food. Then check which bin to use.

facts.title: Stay safe
facts.body: Do not touch broken glass or sharp cans. Step back and tell a grown-up.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005.question: What should a grown-up help do before recycling a jar?
choices: Put it in a plastic bag
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005.explanation: Yes! Ask a grown-up to help empty and rinse it, then check the bin rules.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006.title: Choose food for the soil
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006.intro: Let's choose what belongs in compost. We can help the soil and keep other things out.

facts.title: Leaves belong
facts.body: Dry leaves can go in a compost pile. So can some fruit and vegetable scraps.

facts.title: Plastic stays out
facts.body: Plastic forks and wrappers do not belong in the pile. Ask a grown-up where they go.

facts.title: Ask before you sort
facts.body: Never pick up a battery or an unknown item to sort it. Tell a grown-up and let them help.

10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006.question: Which thing belongs in a compost pile?
10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006.explanation: Yes! Dry leaves belong in compost. Batteries and plastic do not.
